It contains aggregated, non-PII data. Core data elements include number of applicants, county, zip code, inspections, severity of damage, and assistance provided. 

Data is self-reported and subject to human error. For example, when an applicant registers online, they enter their street and city address. title: Summary
text: rfema R package provides simplified interface accessing data U.S. Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) open API. FEMA maintains extensive datasets related disaster risk management, flood insurance claims, hazard mitigation projects, individual assistance programs crucial research natural hazards, policy analysis, emergency management planning. However, accessing datasets directly FEMA’s API can challenging researchers without technical API experience, particularly given API’s 1000-record-per-call limit requires iterative requests complete datasets. rfema package abstracts away complexity API interactions providing intuitive R functions handle authentication-free API calls, automatic pagination large datasets, data cleaning operations including date parsing data type conversions. package enables researchers easily discover available datasets metadata functions, apply filters retrieve specific subsets data, obtain research-ready tibbles properly formatted columns. Key functionality includes accessing National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP) claims policies data, disaster declarations, hazard mitigation assistance records, housing assistance data, among others. eliminating technical barriers FEMA data access, rfema supports reproducible research related natural hazards, flood risk analysis, emergency management.

title: Summary
text: Research natural hazards increasingly relies comprehensive historical data understand patterns natural hazard impacts, evaluate policy effectiveness, inform risk mitigation strategies. FEMA’s open data represents one extensive repositories disaster-related information United States, containing 50 datasets millions records spanning decades disaster response, flood insurance claims, hazard mitigation activities. Historically, FEMA hosted bulk CSV files download, 2025, data can accessed using FEMA API. However, technical complexity API interactions creates significant barrier researchers need data scientific analysis. Existing R packages general API access, httr [@Wickham2020] jsonlite [@Ooms2014], provide low-level functionality require substantial programming expertise handle FEMA’s specific API structure, pagination requirements, data format inconsistencies. Researchers often spend considerable time writing custom scripts manage API calls, handle errors, clean returned data. rfema package fills gap providing domain-specific solution handles FEMA API complexities automatically. Unlike general-purpose API packages, rfema specifically designed FEMA’s data structure includes built-knowledge available datasets, searchable parameters, appropriate data transformations. enables researchers focusing natural hazards, flood risk assessment, climate adaptation, emergency management focus research questions rather data acquisition mechanics. package supports reproducible research practices providing consistent, documented methods data retrieval can easily shared replicated across studies. particularly important natural hazards research, data consistency transparency crucial policy recommendations risk assessments protect lives property.
